findings.title: The Goal still promises lockers in the holds, but after the fix no hold on any shipped ship gets a locker
findings.claim: With the crate first and the fit rule, the Cutter's Upper Hold gets 1 crate and the Skiff Hold gets 1 crate. The Lower Hold and Aft Store get nothing, so no hold on a shipped ship ever shows a locker. The only locker drawn on today's ships is `prop.locker.a` in the Galley. The Goal at L9 still says 'lockers and crates in the holds'.
findings.evidence: spec L9 (Goal), L36 (hold list crate first), L57 (hand count: Upper Hold 1 crate, Skiff Hold 1 crate, Lower Hold and Aft Store none). cutter.json:L10 (Upper Hold S is one row, x=5..7). skiff.json:L12-13 (Hold H is x=7..9, y=6..7); its two remaining candidates (8,6) and (9,7) are diagonal to each other, so the room takes 1 slot.
findings.why: The diff directly caused a small contradiction with an unchanged section. Whoever runs the owner's gate would expect lockers in the holds.
findings.fix: Reword L9 to say 'crates in the holds' (and lockers where a hold is deep enough), or state there that on today's ships lockers only show in the Galley.

findings.title: The depth wording in the fit step can be misread for the e and w sides, and the test's 'names in list order' does not match the take rule
findings.claim: (a) In step 4, '2 x its width for e or w, after the quarter turn' is correct only if 'width' means the turned rectangle's x-extent. That extent is 2 x the art height, matching `consolePlacement`, where e and w use width H=2h. Read as the art's own width, a 66-unit locker on an e or w wall would 'fit' a one-tile room. Also, 'depth from the wall face … minus WALL_GAP' is really the depth past the tile edge. (b) Step 5 gives each candidate the first not-yet-used name that fits it, so a skipped name can go to a later candidate (e.g. crate, crate, locker.a). The test bullet says 'names in list order skipping names that do not fit', and that could be written as a strict order check that fails in this case.
findings.evidence: spec L54 (fit wording), L55 (first not-yet-used fitting name), L71 (test wording). consoleModel.ts:L107-L112: e and w boxes use width H = 2*h, so depth is always 2 x the art height.
findings.why: No shipped ship hits either case: every e or w candidate is in a room 3 tiles deep, and the Skiff Hold takes one slot. A fresh implementer could still code the wrong reading or write a brittle test.
findings.fix: In step 4, say 'depth = 2 x the art height minus WALL_GAP for every side (the turned rectangle's extent perpendicular to the wall)'. In the test bullet, say 'each slot's name is the first not-yet-used name of the room's list that fits it'.

prior.note: The hold list now starts with `prop.crate` (L36), and step 4 (L54) adds a fit rule that matches `consolePlacement` geometry. For the Upper Hold, the candidates are (6,3) and (7,3), both with side n, one tile deep. The crate's depth is 2*16-10=22 <= 32, so it fits. The locker's is 2*33-10=56 > 32, so it is skipped. The crate's rectangle is y -10..22 and x 4..28 in tile-local units, which stays inside the room. The outcomes at L57 match a hand count for both the Cutter and the Skiff. The new test at L71 checks that no prop crosses another wall's face. Two P3 wording points remain, listed under findings.

verified: Upper Hold candidates: the lamp tile (5,3) is also excluded by the O-S door (4,3), the S-a door (5,4) and the breach (5,2). That leaves (6,3) and (7,3), side n first, adjacent to each other, so 1 slot (cutter.json:L10-11, L119-158, L339-345).
Crate placement flush north: consolePlacement('n', true, 12, 16) gives left=even(16-12)=4, top=-10, width 24, height 32, inside the tile and the wall gap (consoleModel.ts:L106-L114, L20).
Locker on side n: depth 66-10=56 > 32, so it fails the fit rule in a one-tile room, and the rule matches the geometry (bottom edge H-gap compared against 32n).

Skiff Hold: excluding (7,6) lamp, (9,6) door neighbour, (7,7) breach neighbour and (8,7) airlock neighbour leaves (8,6) side n (2 deep) and (9,7) side e (3 deep). They are diagonal, so 1 slot, and the crate fits either (skiff.json:L12-13, L32, L44, L62).
Lower Hold and Aft Store still have no candidates: the magazine (6,9), the doors (4,9), (5,8) and (2,8), and the breach (1,10) exclude every wall tile (cutter.json:L15, L159-188, L379-385, L581).
Crew Quarters and Galley are 3x3, so every listed prop fits (deepest 56 <= 96). The fit rule leaves the R2-confirmed counts of 2 and 3 unchanged.

Lateral overhang: the widest prop (seats, 50 units) spans tile-local x -10..40. That lies within the wall faces at -10 and 42 when both side neighbours are walls, so on rectangular rooms nothing crosses a side wall.
not_verified: I did not recheck whether the 'never crosses a wall other than its own' claim at L54 holds for non-rectangular rooms, where a wide prop's overhang into a neighbouring column with shallower floor could cross a wall. Every shipped room is rectangular, and the new test would catch it if a layout ever hit this.
I did not re-view the sprite rectangles on the sheets this round, since section 1 is unchanged.
